scope: Hardware comparison against last commit; no new component or copper changes during this review. No supplier contact or order.
judgment: Cost-reduced prototype with unchanged intended speed and core function. Thermal/saturation margin and connector contact margin are lower. No new connectivity or high-speed-route failure was identified. Existing VDD transient and power-cycle risks prevent promising first-spin success.

changes.assessment: Reduced thermal and saturation margin. TI lists this Murata family as a TPS62903 candidate. It passes the current static/LC/current screens, but board temperature and closed-loop behavior remain unqualified.
changes.tenPercentDropCriterion: No Murata rating published in available specification; unknown, not a pass.

changes.assessment: Same mechanical lands and PCIe family. Gold plating falls from 30 to 15 microinch, reducing contact wear/corrosion margin; no intended lane-count or speed reduction. No mating-cycle guarantee inferred.

Values/topology checked against the built netlist. VCCL feedback becomes 26.2k rather than 26.1k; the calculated static range remains 1.85 to 1.95 V. Slot 3.3 V on RC changes about +0.0184%, and off RC about -7.1%. Precision replacements improve resistor tolerance. Two 10 uF VCCA33 capacitors replace one 22 uF part; the tolerance-only minimum improves slightly, but effective operating capacitance remains conditional.

Removed LED, buffer and their support parts. This removes status visibility; the old indicator did not control power sequencing. PSU_ACCESS provides unpopulated GND/5V/PWR_OK holes. R_PSU_ON is still the ATX start jumper.

nativePlacement.advisory: C_VDD_28 suboptimal orientation, unchanged since HEAD.
nativePlacement.disposition: Reviewed as a nearest-connected-port placement heuristic, not an actual copper-crossing report. CLI implementation does not inspect routed copper for this advisory. Existing capacitor position, rotation and pad geometry match HEAD; actual routing, continuity, shorts and spacing audits pass. Rotating the already-routed capacitor is not warranted by this heuristic alone.

campaignFailureExplanation: The original audit coerced an absent Murata 10%-drop rating to zero. Corrected diagnostics retain UNQUALIFIED rather than asserting a failure or a pass.
Heatsink check lacked the Yageo RT0402 body dimensions. Added the manufacturer maximum height; rerun passes the same offset.
PSU access silkscreen changed while the campaign ran. A fresh full build proves all electrical and physical copper entities match; only silkscreen graphics and generated warning counter text differ.
verification.staleHeatsinkArtifact: Original campaign retained an older report after the failed stage. That report is not current-board fit evidence. Follow-up evidence is source-bound; the runner now removes old expected output files before each stage.
powerModelCorrections: Inductance ripple sensitivities now follow each selected inductor: HEAD 0.72 to 1.2 uH, current 0.504 to 1.2 uH. These are sensitivity bounds, not guaranteed combined operating specifications.
Follow-up binds computed 5 V feed loss: current input lower bounds 4.68345 V VCCL and 4.67695 V VDD, including conservative 2 A per-input copper stress.
Reset campaign now binds the selected board.

findings.origin: pre-existing, slightly less margin with new inductors
findings.title: VDD load-step robustness remains unqualified
findings.evidence: With the same provisional 3 A VDD load and prescribed regulator response, the selected 1.5-to-3 A step leaves 0.365 mV lower margin after ripple; release leaves 0.431 mV upper margin. HEAD gives 0.614 and 0.619 mV. Broader assumed corners leave the allowed voltage window in both designs.
findings.limit: These are passive-network sensitivity calculations, not a TPS62903 closed-loop prediction or measured waveforms. The numbers cannot establish actual bridge stability.
findings.nextCheck: Measure both load-step directions at the bridge power lands and verify the regulator response with the assembled output network.

findings.title: Short power interruptions are outside the qualified operating envelope
findings.evidence: HEAD and current reset simulation results are exactly identical. 68 of 96 passive cycle cases fail to reach the guaranteed reset-low level before return. The unchanged 12 V switch forced-return model exceeds its recorded 70 A pulse ceiling; the blocking-source study still reaches about 159 A. The paired 3.3 V comparison retains the same four outside-SOA scenarios.
findings.limit: Supply return ramps, semiconductor temperature, card capacitance and SOA extension are assumptions. Settling does not prove safe restart.
findings.nextCheck: Evaluate reset discharge/supervision and gate restart control; measure real supply-return waveforms. Use cold card installation and avoid rapid cycling during bring-up.

findings.title: Inductor thermal and inductance headroom is lower
findings.evidence: Max DCR rises from 9 to 40 milliohm, adding about 0.28 W copper loss per coil at 3 A and 25 C. Published 40 C-rise current falls from 12 A to 3.3 A under vendor test conditions. The original 10%-drop criterion is unknown for Murata.
findings.limit: Vendor ratings use different test boards and are not a board-specific temperature prediction. Core losses and actual airflow are not included in that copper-loss estimate.
findings.nextCheck: Measure coil temperature, switch waveform and rail ripple at sustained maximum load, especially VDD.

findings.title: Cooling, BGA assembly and full channel operation remain unproven
findings.evidence: Offset heatsink fit passes the corrected body-envelope check, conditional on a base at least 0.8 mm above PCB. Accepted bridge rail allowances total 5.62 W; actual heat/airflow and package height require verification. Manufacturer acceptance of the BGA process is not recorded. USB4/PCIe channel models omit parts of the complete channel and do not establish eye/BER compliance.
findings.nextCheck: Verify the actual cooling fixture and BGA assembly process; measure link speed/error behavior on hardware.

findings.title: VCCL 3 A conductor stress screen remains open
findings.evidence: Upper 80 C mesh drop is 17.699 mV now versus 17.573 mV in HEAD, against an 8 mV project target. The accepted planning current is 1 A, where the linear conductor estimate meets that target.
findings.limit: The 1 A VCCL and 3 A VDD budgets are provisional and unmeasured.
